calls.head: The Senators should drive the play
calls.body: The Senators have been near the top of the league at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Sharks one of the worst. Expect the Senators to spend more of the night in the Sharks’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

calls.body: The Senators keep dangerous shots away, but the Sharks give up a lot of them. Ottawa is near the top of the league for preventing dangerous shots, and San Jose is near the bottom. The more dangerous chances should come at the Sharks’ net.

surprises.head: Ottawa buried San Jose in shots
surprises.body: San Jose allows more shots than almost anyone. Even by those standards, this was lopsided: Ottawa took 61 of the 88 shot attempts at 5-on-5. From how these two usually play, Ottawa would expect about 53%. A team strays this far about once every 200 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

story.head: The Senators cruise past the Sharks
paras: Dylan Cozens got the scoring started for the Senators midway through the first. Michael Misa tied it 1-1 for San Jose less than three minutes later, but the Sharks didn’t score again. Drake Batherson restored the Senators’ lead early in the second, and Tim Stützle made it 3-1 midway through the period. Ridly Greig stretched the lead to 4-1 shorthanded less than two minutes later. Shane Pinto added an empty-net goal with two and a half minutes left to make it 5-1. Philip Tomasino made his Senators debut, after two seasons with the Penguins, and picked up an assist.

The Senators drove the play, outshooting the Sharks 35-23, and the scoreboard caught up. Samuel Ersson made 22 saves for the Sens, and Alex Nedeljkovic stopped 30 of 34 at the other end. Nobody on the ice had a bigger night than Jake Sanderson, by our Swing measure.

Kiefer Sherwood picked up a ten-minute misconduct. The Sharks killed off a two-man advantage that lasted two minutes early in the third. The Senators improved to 9-5-1 and climbed to third in the Atlantic, while the Sharks fell to 7-7-1, fourth in the Pacific.
